# Template: heatmap
A heatmap: a grid of cells whose FILL DENSITY is the number — one row drawable per matrix row (`row_1`, `row_2`, …) so a reveal can walk down it. `rows` and `cols` name the axes, `values` is a 2-D grid (row-major, one list per row), and every cell carries its own number unless `value_labels: false`. `scale: "sequential"` (default) washes one ink from the low end of the data to the high — counts, rates, a confusion matrix; `scale: "diverging"` uses TWO inks either side of zero, warm above and cool below, both normalised by the largest absolute value — a correlation matrix, a difference table, anything where the sign is the story. `values` may also be a list of GRIDS — stages of the same matrix — and the numeric `stage` param picks which one is shown; a fractional stage interpolates, so `animate: {stage: 1}` plays the change as the wash deepening and fading. The scale is fixed across every stage, so the colours never flicker mid-tween. `animate` is the ONLY way to move a staged heatmap: this scene has no stage slider in the explore tray, because the tray cannot yet tell a matrix from stages of a matrix. `box` puts the grid somewhere other than the whole plot — beside a code panel, usually — and everything but the title then lives inside it. Write `null` for a masked cell (the upper triangle of a correlation matrix, a combination that cannot happen): it draws as blank rather than as a fabricated zero. Feed it typed numbers, or a code element's variables via "{id.var}" tokens (type the row and column names by hand so the row_i beats exist before the script has run). Choose this scene for ANY request for a heatmap, a correlation matrix, a confusion matrix, a transition or migration matrix, a risk matrix, a cross-tabulation shown as colour, or "which combinations are highest". At most 12 rows × 12 columns — past that a cell is too small to hold its own number, and the scene says so on the canvas.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the grid's rule and the column names along its top
- row_1: the first row of cells — its wash, its numbers and its row name (row_2, row_3, … likewise); draw them one per beat to walk down the matrix
- legend: the scale — which wash means which number
- note: the refusal note — drawn when the matrix is bigger than 12 × 12, and when an authored `box` is too small to hold the grid (in that case it is the ONLY thing drawn besides the title)
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Correlation matrix of age, income, BMI and blood pressure." → params: {"rows":["Age","Income","BMI","Blood pressure"],"cols":["Age","Income","BMI","Blood pressure"],"values":[[1,-0.12,0.34,0.51],[-0.12,1,0.08,-0.21],[0.34,0.08,1,0.46],[0.51,-0.21,0.46,1]],"scale":"diverging","decimals":2,"title":"What moves with what"}
Request: "Show the confusion matrix from the classifier I fit in Python." → params: {"rows":["Actual: no","Actual: yes"],"cols":["Predicted: no","Predicted: yes"],"values":"{clf.cm}","decimals":0,"title":"Confusion matrix"}
Request: "Compute the correlation matrix with pandas and show it next to the code." → params: {"rows":["Age","BMI","Systolic"],"cols":["Age","BMI","Systolic"],"values":"{corr.m}","scale":"diverging","decimals":2,"box":{"x":470,"y":95,"w":460,"h":560},"title":"What pandas found"}

In YAML: `template: heatmap` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
